title: Recording with Sidney Bechet and Clarence Williams
summary: She recalls the 1924 sessions with Clarence Williams and Bechet, "Off and On Blues" and records later sent by Williams's son.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well now, you played in 1924 with Clarence Williams?
And those records you made in New York? Right?
Do you remember when Sidney Bechet played with you?
Yeah, I remember (unintelligible). I liked Bechet playing. I love his (unintelligible). I like a sax.
The tunes you did with Bechet and Clarence Williams and Buddy Christian on the banjo, 'I'm So Glad I'm Brown Skinned,'
(Unintelligible) he sent me about six records.
Oh, yeah? That was nice of him.
That one, he say, 'Sippie,' he say, 'We got some of your records, I thought maybe you'd want to have.'
How about 'Off and On Blues', did you
get that one? Because Bechet was on that one, too.
Yeah, that made a big hit. That was one of the (unintelligible) said, Sippie, you got a real hit "Off and On Blues" on the way. He said (unintelligible). And I had forgot about it.
I had done forgot about it. So he made Bechet?
Yeah, Bechet was on that one with you.
I didn't know Bechet was on it. I got it.
(Unintelligible) and somebody sent them to the (unintelligible).
And did you pick the ones you wanted?
